To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the formation of the r-process elements is very sensitive to the cooling law of the neutrino-driven winds, and that a fast but continuing cooling at large radii allows to produce more heavy r-process elements than in the case of a slower cooling or constant density.
the third abundance peak in neutrino-driven winds is sensitive to the transition temperature and to the cooling law during the late, slow evolution phase.
the transition temperature and the subsequent cooling law in the r-process environment can be as important for the formation of the third peak as the entropy and the initial proton-to-baryron ratio.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the sensitivity of the r-process path on the expansion behavior of the outflow, and with the possible influence of a transition between a fast and a slow expansion on the formation of the third r-process abundance peak.
the question how the dynamics of the outflow affects its r-process nucleosynthetic outcome, in particular the production of the platinum peak.

the question of whether the dynamics of proto- neutron star winds, in particular their transition to a slower phase, may be responsible for a strong enhancement of the r-process abundance at mass numbers A ≈ 195.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the r-processing in neutrino-driven winds is very sensitive to the expansion timescales and the temperature behavior of the outflow, and thus to the dynamical evolution of the outflow.
the formation of the third peak is more sensitive to the expansion timescale and cooling law during the second, slow phase of the wind evolution than to the initial conditions of the outflow.
a fast cooling and a low transition temperature are favorable for r-process nucleosynthetic yields.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the formation of the third abundance maximum is more sensitive to the cooling behavior of the outflow than the production of the second one, but that the production of the first peak is more sensitive to a change in the expansion behavior of the out-flow.

the r-process nucleosynthetic yields in neutrino-driven winds can be very sensitive to the details of the expansion history of the outflows and that the transition temperature and cooling law during the second phase can make a big impact on the production of the third abundance maximum.

a fast, exponential decline in temperature during the early expansion phase, as expected in the presence of a strong decelerating wind termination shock, may be favorable to r-process nucleosyntheses in the region of A > 130, but only if the subsequent evolution of temperature and density does not become too slow.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the r-process nucleosynthetic outcome is very sensitive to the details of the outflow dynamics and thermodynamics, and in particular to the cooling and expansion behavior at large distances from the compact object.

the expansion timescale and the transition temperature are the most important parameters for the r-process nucleosynthetic outcome, and that a fast transition to a slower expansion phase can be beneficial for the formation of a third abundance peak, if the cooling is not too strong in the temperature range between 2 × 108 and 10 9K.
a detailed understanding of the wind dynamics is crucial for the understanding of the r-process nucleosynthetic yields, in particular of the third abundance plateau.
